prompt: Which approach matches CSL Group's design?
scenario: A shipping company has 40 vessels with expensive, unreliable satellite links. Shore teams need fuel and alarm data quickly, but also want detailed machinery history for analysis.

options.text: Edge Data Store on board; send critical data in near real time and upload non-critical data later
Stream every tag at full resolution over satellite all the time
Collect data only when ships are in port
Keep all data on each ship and never send it ashore

explanation: CSL uses AVEVA Edge Data Store to capture data onboard, sends critical data by satellite in near real time and uploads non-critical data later. It reported up to 50% upload bandwidth reduction.

prompt: Which outcomes does the CSL Group success story report? Select all that apply.

options.text: 8,233 mt CO2e avoided across 11 vessels in a year (third-party verified)
29% carbon intensity reduction
"over 300" anomaly detections
Up to 50% upload bandwidth reduction
About $450,000 per vessel per year from barnacle removal

explanation: The first four are CSL figures. About $450,000 per vessel per year from timing barnacle removal is Caterpillar.

prompt: True or false: Cargill ships store data locally when out of network range, using Edge Data Store and an AVEVA Adapter for Modbus.

options.text: True
False

explanation: True. The Cargill story says its ships store data locally when out of range, using Edge Data Store and an AVEVA Adapter for Modbus.

prompt: Caterpillar notes fuel is nearly ___% of a RORO vessel's lifetime cost.
explanation: Caterpillar notes fuel is nearly 70% of a RORO vessel's lifetime cost, and vessels may operate for about 50 years.

prompt: What saving does AVEVA report for Caterpillar from timing barnacle removal?

options.text: About $450,000 per vessel per year
About $10,000 per vessel per year
$25M in fiscal 2017
8,233 mt CO2e per vessel

explanation: About $450,000 per vessel per year from timing barnacle removal (hull fouling). About $10,000 is the 2018 cruise-liner cylinder temperature catch, a one-off; $25M is DCP Midstream; 8,233 mt CO2e is CSL across 11 vessels.

prompt: Which marine outcome is described as third-party verified?

options.text: CSL's 8,233 mt CO2e avoided across 11 vessels
Caterpillar's $450,000 per vessel per year
Delfi's reduced training cost
CSL's over 300 anomaly detections

explanation: Only the CSL CO2e figure is described as third-party verified. Most success-story figures are reported by the vendor and not independently audited.

prompt: Match each marine term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Marine growth that increases drag and fuel burn
CO2 emitted per unit of transport work

explanation: These are the definitions used with the Caterpillar and CSL sources.

prompt: What did CSL find about biofuel energy content?

options.text: It was 12-15% lower than conventional fuel, needing more fuel per unit of performance
It was 12-15% higher than conventional fuel
It was identical to marine gas oil
It cut fuel use by 29%

explanation: CSL found biofuel energy content 12-15% lower than conventional fuel. The 29% figure is CSL's carbon intensity reduction.

prompt: Which data problems do the marine sources name? Select all that apply.

options.text: Limited, unreliable bandwidth
Frequent crew turnover causing inconsistent data
Onboard data silos preventing cross-fleet learning
Weather and ocean noise in the data
Too many AF elements per vessel

explanation: CSL names bandwidth and crew turnover; Caterpillar names onboard silos and weather/ocean noise. No source mentions too many AF elements.
